title: Optional Chaining and Nullish Coalescing
summary: Optional chaining (?.) safely accesses nested properties or calls methods without throwing if an intermediate value is null or undefined — it short-circuits and returns undefined instead. Nullish coalescing (??) provides a fallback value only when the left side is null or undefined. It is stricter than || which also falls back for 0, '', and false — this matters when 0 is a valid value (e.g. a movie rating of 0).
keyPoints: movie?.director?.name — returns undefined if movie or director is null/undefined, no throw
?? provides a fallback only for null or undefined
|| provides a fallback for any falsy value: null, undefined, 0, '', false
Use ?? for ratings and counts where 0 is valid data
Use || only when you want to fall back on all falsy values

exercises.prompt:
Given:
const movie = { title: 'Unknown' }  // no director field

What does movie.director?.name return?
exercises.explanation: movie.director is undefined. The ?. operator short-circuits and returns undefined without throwing. Without ?., movie.director.name would throw TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined.

exercises.prompt: What is the difference between ?? and || when used as a fallback operator?
options: ?? only falls back for null/undefined; || falls back for any falsy value (0, '', false, null, undefined)
|| only falls back for null/undefined; ?? falls back for any falsy value
?? throws for falsy values; || does not
exercises.answer: ?? only falls back for null/undefined; || falls back for any falsy value (0, '', false, null, undefined)
exercises.explanation: This distinction matters: rating || 'N/A' would replace a rating of 0 with 'N/A', which is wrong. rating ?? 'N/A' keeps 0 because 0 is not null or undefined.

exercises.prompt: Given vote_average = 0, which expression correctly displays the rating without replacing 0 with a fallback?
exercises.explanation: ?? only triggers on null or undefined. 0 is a valid rating, not a missing value — ?? keeps it. || treats 0 as falsy and would incorrectly replace it with 'N/A'.

exercises.prompt:
Given:
const movie2 = { title: 'Unknown' }  // no cast field

How do you safely get the name of the first cast member, with 'Unknown cast' as a fallback?
exercises.explanation: Each step that could be null/undefined needs its own ?.: movie2?, then cast?, then [0]?, then name. Without ?. on cast, accessing [0] on undefined would still throw.

exercises.prompt: A TMDB movie has poster_path: null. Which expression returns the correct placeholder URL?
exercises.explanation: null triggers both || and ??. Since poster_path is directly on movie (movie itself exists), both B and C work. C adds optional chaining for safety if movie itself might be null. In practice, if movie is guaranteed to exist, B and C are equivalent here.

exercises.prompt: When is optional chaining (?.) especially important when working with the TMDB API?
options: When accessing nested fields that may be null or absent in the API response
exercises.answer: When accessing nested fields that may be null or absent in the API response
exercises.explanation: TMDB API responses regularly have nullable fields: poster_path, backdrop_path, belongs_to_collection, tagline. Optional chaining lets you access them safely without defensive if-checks at every level.
|| falls back for any falsy value, including an empty string ''. ?? only falls back for null or undefined — it would return '' unchanged because '' is not null or undefined.

exercises.prompt:
Given:
const movie2 = { title: 'Unknown Film' }  // no cast field

What does movie2.cast?.[0]?.name return?
exercises.explanation: movie2.cast is undefined. The ?. before [0] short-circuits and returns undefined without attempting to access index 0 on undefined. The whole chain safely evaluates to undefined.
